units.Micah 1:1: The word of the Lord came to Michaiah of Morashthi in the days of Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, concerning what he saw about Samaria and Jerusalem.
units.Micah 1:2: Hear words, you peoples! Let the earth and everyone in it attend! The Lord will be among you as a testimony, the Lord from His holy house.
units.Micah 1:3: For look, the Lord is coming out of His place; He will descend and step upon the heights of the earth,
units.Micah 1:4: and the mountains will be shaken beneath Him, and the valleys will melt like wax before fire and like water flowing downhill.
units.Micah 1:5: All this is because of Jacob’s impiety and the sin of Israel’s house. What is Jacob’s impiety? Is it not Samaria? And what is the sin of Judah’s house? Is it not Jerusalem?
units.Micah 1:6: I will make Samaria a fruit watcher’s hut in a field and a vineyard plantation. I will pull her stones down into a chasm and uncover her foundations.
units.Micah 1:7: They will cut up all her carved images and burn all her wages in fire, and I will consign all her idols to obliteration. For she gathered from prostitution wages and amassed from prostitution wages.
units.Micah 1:8: Because of this she will lament and mourn; she will go barefoot and naked. She will make lamentation like dragons and mourning like daughters of sirens.
units.Micah 1:9: For her blow has prevailed; it came as far as Judah and touched the gate of My people, as far as Jerusalem.
units.Micah 1:10: You in Gath, do not magnify yourselves! You in Akim, do not rebuild from a house for laughter; sprinkle yourselves with earth in keeping with your laughter.
units.Micah 1:11: Dwelling well in her cities, the inhabitant of Sennaan did not come out to mourn the house adjoining her; she will receive from you a blow of pain.
units.Micah 1:12: Who began good things for the woman dwelling in pains? For calamities came down from the Lord upon Jerusalem’s gates,
units.Micah 1:13: the noise of chariots and horsemen. Inhabitant of Lachish, she is a leader of sin to the daughter of Zion, for Israel’s impieties were found in you.
units.Micah 1:14: Therefore you will give away those being sent as far as the inheritance of Gath—vain houses; it became empty things for Israel’s kings.
units.Micah 1:15: Until I bring heirs to you, O inheritance dwelling in Lachish, the glory of Israel’s daughter will come as far as Odollam.
units.Micah 1:16: Shave yourself and shear your hair for your delicate children. Enlarge your widowhood like an eagle, for they have been taken captive away from you.
units.Micah 2:1: They became people planning troubles and working evil on their beds, and at daybreak they carried them out, because they did not raise their hands to God.
units.Micah 2:2: They coveted fields and plundered orphans, oppressed houses and plundered a man and his house, a man and his inheritance.
units.Micah 2:3: Therefore thus says the Lord: “Look, I am planning calamities against this tribe, from which you will certainly not lift your necks, and you will certainly not suddenly walk upright, for it is an evil time.
units.Micah 2:4: On that day a parable will be taken up against you, and a lament will be sung in melody, saying: ‘We have suffered grievous misery! The portion of My people was measured with a cord, and there was no one to prevent him from turning away; our fields were divided.’
units.Micah 2:5: Therefore you will have no one casting a measuring cord by lot in the assembly of the Lord.
units.Micah 2:6: Do not weep with tears, nor let them shed tears over these things, for he will not reject reproaches.
units.Micah 2:7: The one who says, ‘Jacob’s house has provoked the Lord’s Spirit’: Are these his practices? Are not his words good with him, and have they walked uprightly?
units.Micah 2:8: And formerly My people stood opposed in enmity; facing his peace, they flayed his skin to take away hope—a shattering of war.
units.Micah 2:9: Therefore the leaders of My people will be cast out of their luxurious houses; because of their evil practices they were expelled. Draw near to everlasting mountains!
units.Micah 2:10: Rise and go, for this is no resting place for you because of uncleanness. You were corrupted with corruption,
units.Micah 2:11: you were pursued with no one pursuing. A spirit established falsehood; it dripped to you into wine and strong drink. And it will be from the drop of this people:
units.Micah 2:12: Jacob will surely be gathered with everyone. I will surely receive Israel’s remaining ones; I will put their turning back together. Like sheep in affliction, like a flock within their resting place, they will leap out from among people.
units.Micah 2:13: Through the breach before them they broke through, passed a gate and went out through it. Their king went out before them, and the Lord will lead them.”
units.Micah 3:1: He will say: “Hear these things now, authorities of Jacob’s house and remaining ones of Israel’s house! Is it not for you to know justice,
units.Micah 3:2: you who hate good things and seek evil things, who snatch their skins from them and their flesh from their bones?”
units.Micah 3:3: Just as they ate the flesh of My people, flayed their skins from their bones, crushed their bones and divided them into pieces like flesh for a cauldron and meat for a cooking pot,
units.Micah 3:4: so they will cry to the Lord, but He will not listen to them. He will turn His face away from them at that time, because they acted wickedly in their practices against them.
units.Micah 3:5: Thus says the Lord concerning the prophets who lead My people astray, who bite with their teeth and proclaim peace to him; but when nothing was put into their mouths, they raised war against him:
units.Micah 3:6: “Therefore you will have night instead of vision and darkness instead of divination; the sun will set upon the prophets, and the day will darken over them.
units.Micah 3:7: Those seeing dreams will be ashamed and the diviners mocked; all of them will speak against them, because there will be no one listening to them,
units.Micah 3:8: unless I fill up strength in the Spirit of the Lord and of judgment and might, to declare to Jacob his impieties and to Israel his sins.”
units.Micah 3:9: Hear these things now, leaders of Jacob’s house and remaining ones of Israel’s house, who abhor justice and twist all straight things,
units.Micah 3:10: you who build Zion with bloodshed and Jerusalem with injustices!
units.Micah 3:11: Her leaders judged with gifts, her priests answered for wages and her prophets divined for silver; yet they relied upon the Lord, saying, “Is not the Lord among us? Calamities will certainly not come upon us.”
units.Micah 3:12: Therefore, because of you, Zion will be plowed like a field, Jerusalem will be like a fruit watcher’s hut, and the mountain of the house like a forest grove.
units.Micah 4:1: In the last days the mountain of the Lord will be manifest, established upon the mountain summits and raised above the hills, and peoples will hurry toward it.
units.Micah 4:2: Many nations will go and say, “Come, let us go up to the Lord’s mountain and to the house of Jacob’s God. They will show us His way, and we will walk in His paths.” For law will go out from Zion, and the Lord’s word from Jerusalem.
units.Micah 4:3: He will judge between many peoples and reprove strong nations as far as a distant land. They will cut their swords into plows and their spears into sickles. Nation will certainly no longer raise sword against nation, nor will they learn to wage war anymore.
units.Micah 4:4: Each will rest beneath his vine and each beneath his fig tree, and there will be no one causing fear, because the mouth of the Lord Almighty has spoken these things.
units.Micah 4:5: For all the peoples will walk, each his own way, but we will walk in the name of the Lord our God forever and beyond.
units.Micah 4:6: “On that day,” says the Lord, “I will gather the crushed one, receive the expelled one and those I rejected.
units.Micah 4:7: I will make the crushed one a remnant and the rejected one a strong nation. The Lord will reign over them on Mount Zion from now and forever.
units.Micah 4:8: And you, squalid tower of the flock, daughter of Zion, to you it will come and enter—the former rule, a kingdom from Babylon for the daughter of Jerusalem.”
units.Micah 4:9: And now why have you experienced calamities? Did you have no king? Has your counsel perished, that birth pains have seized you like a woman giving birth?
units.Micah 4:10: Labor in birth, be courageous and draw near, daughter of Zion, like a woman giving birth! For now you will go out from the city, camp in the plain and come as far as Babylon. From there He will rescue you, and from there the Lord your God will redeem you from your enemies’ hand.
units.Micah 4:11: Now many nations have gathered against you, saying, “We will rejoice over her, and our eyes will look upon Zion!”
units.Micah 4:12: But they did not know the Lord’s thought or understand His counsel, for He gathered them like sheaves of a threshing floor.
units.Micah 4:13: Rise and thresh them, daughter of Zion, for I will make your horns iron and your hooves bronze. With them you will melt down nations and grind many peoples fine; you will dedicate their multitude to the Lord and their strength to the Lord of all the earth.
units.Micah 4:14: Now the daughter of Ephraim will be fenced in with a barrier; he has set a constraint upon us. With a rod they will strike Israel’s tribes on the cheek.
units.Micah 5:1: And you, Bethlehem, house of Ephrathah, are small to be among Judah’s thousands; from you one will come out for Me to be a ruler in Israel, and his goings out are from the beginning, from days of old.
units.Micah 5:2: Therefore he will give them up until the time of the woman giving birth, when she gives birth; then the remaining ones of their brothers will return to the sons of Israel.
units.Micah 5:3: He will stand, see and shepherd his flock in the Lord’s strength, and they will exist in the glory of the name of the Lord their God; for now he will be magnified to the ends of the earth.
units.Micah 5:4: This will be peace: when an Assyrian comes upon your land and steps upon your country, seven shepherds and eight bites of people will rise against him.
units.Micah 5:5: They will shepherd Assour with the sword and Nebrod’s land in its ditch. He will rescue from Assour when he comes upon your land and steps upon your borders.
units.Micah 5:6: Jacob’s remnant will be among the nations, amid many peoples, like dew falling from the Lord and like lambs upon couch grass, so that no one may be gathered or stand among the sons of humankind.
units.Micah 5:7: Jacob’s remnant will be among the nations, amid many peoples, like a lion among beasts in the forest and like a young lion among flocks of sheep, which passes through, separates and seizes, with no one to deliver.
units.Micah 5:8: Your hand will be raised above those afflicting you, and all your enemies will be destroyed.
units.Micah 5:9: “On that day,” says the Lord, “I will destroy your horses from your midst and destroy your chariots,
units.Micah 5:10: and I will destroy the cities of your land and remove all your strongholds.
units.Micah 5:11: I will remove your sorceries from your hands, and there will be no utterers of oracles among you.
units.Micah 5:12: I will destroy your carved images and pillars from your midst, and you will certainly no longer bow down to the works of your hands.
units.Micah 5:13: I will cut down your groves from your midst and obliterate your cities.
units.Micah 5:14: I will execute vengeance in anger and wrath among the nations because they did not obey.”
units.Micah 6:1: Hear now the word of the Lord. The Lord said: “Rise, enter into judgment before the mountains, and let the hills hear your voice.”
units.Micah 6:2: Hear, hills, the Lord’s judgment, and you ravines, foundations of the earth! For the Lord has a case against His people, and He will argue it with Israel.
units.Micah 6:3: “My people, what have I done to you? How have I grieved you, or how have I troubled you? Answer Me!
units.Micah 6:4: For I brought you up from Egypt’s land and redeemed you from the house of slavery. I sent Moses, Aaron and Miriam before you.
units.Micah 6:5: My people, remember what Balak king of Moab planned against you and what Balaam son of Beor answered him, from the rushes to Galgal, so that the Lord’s righteousness may be known.”
units.Micah 6:6: With what shall I take hold of the Lord and grasp my God Most High? Shall I take hold of Him with whole burnt offerings, with year-old calves?
units.Micah 6:7: Will the Lord receive with thousands of rams or with ten thousands of fat-rich torrents? Shall I give my firstborn offspring for impieties, the fruit of my body for the sin of my life?
units.Micah 6:8: Has it been declared to you, O man, what is good? Or what does the Lord seek from you, except to do justice, and to love mercy, and to be ready to walk with the Lord your God?
units.Micah 6:9: The Lord’s voice will be called to the city, and He will save those who fear His name. “Hear, tribe! And who will adorn a city?
units.Micah 6:10: Is there not fire, and a lawless person’s house storing lawless treasures, and injustice with insolence?
units.Micah 6:11: Will a lawless person be justified with a balance and deceptive weights in a pouch?
units.Micah 6:12: From these they filled their wealth with impiety; those inhabiting her spoke falsehoods, and their tongue was exalted in their mouth.
units.Micah 6:13: And I will begin to strike you; I will obliterate you because of your sins.
units.Micah 6:14: You will eat but certainly not be filled. It will grow dark within you and turn aside, and you will certainly not be saved; whoever is saved will be handed over to the sword.
units.Micah 6:15: You will sow but certainly not reap; you will press olives but certainly not anoint yourself with oil, and you will press wine, but you shall certainly not drink it. The ordinances of My people will be obliterated.
units.Micah 6:16: You kept the ordinances of Zambri and all the works of Achaab’s house, and you walked in their counsels, so that I may hand you over to obliteration and her inhabitants to hissing. You will receive the reproaches of peoples.”
units.Micah 7:1: Alas! I have become like someone gathering stubble at harvest and a gleaning at vintage, with no cluster available to eat the first fruits. Alas, my soul,
units.Micah 7:2: for the devout person has perished from the earth, and no one acts rightly among people. They all litigate for bloodshed; each crushes his neighbor with crushing.
units.Micah 7:3: They prepare their hands for evil; the ruler asks, and the judge spoke peaceful words—it is his soul’s desire. And I will remove
units.Micah 7:4: their good things like a moth eating away and walking upon a measuring rod on the day of watching. Woe, woe! Your punishments have arrived; now they will weep.
units.Micah 7:5: Do not put confidence in friends or hope in leaders. With your bed companion, beware of entrusting anything to her.
units.Micah 7:6: For a son dishonors his father, a daughter will rise against her mother, a daughter-in-law will rise against her mother-in-law; a man’s enemies are all the men in his house.
units.Micah 7:7: But I will look toward the Lord; I will wait upon God my Savior. My God will listen to me.
units.Micah 7:8: Do not rejoice over me, my enemy, because I have fallen! I will rise, for if I sit in darkness, the Lord will shine for me.
units.Micah 7:9: I will bear the Lord’s anger, for I sinned against Him, until He vindicates my case. He will execute my judgment and bring me out into the light; I will see His righteousness.
units.Micah 7:10: My enemy will see and clothe herself in shame, she who says to me, “Where is the Lord your God?” My eyes will look upon her; now she will become a trampling place like mud in the streets
units.Micah 7:11: on a day of brick plastering. That day is your obliteration, and it will rub away your ordinances—
units.Micah 7:12: that day. Your cities will come to leveling and division among Assyrians, and your fortified cities to division from Tyre as far as Syria’s river—a day of water and tumult.
units.Micah 7:13: The land will become an obliteration together with those inhabiting it, from the fruits of their practices.
units.Micah 7:14: Shepherd Thy people with Thy rod, the sheep of Thine inheritance, camping by themselves in a forest amid Carmel. They will graze in Bashan and Gilead as in the days of old.
units.Micah 7:15: And as in the days of your departure from Egypt, you will see wonderful things.
units.Micah 7:16: Nations will see and be ashamed of all their strength. They will place hands over their mouth; their ears will be deafened.
units.Micah 7:17: They will lick dust like snakes dragging along the earth; they will be thrown into turmoil in their confinement. They will be astonished at the Lord our God and fear Thee.
units.Micah 7:18: Who is a God like Thee, removing injustices and passing over impieties for the remaining ones of His inheritance? He did not retain His anger as a testimony, because He desires mercy.
units.Micah 7:19: He Himself will turn back and pity us; He will sink our injustices, and they will be thrown into the depths of the sea—all our sins.
units.Micah 7:20: Thou wilt grant truth to Jacob, mercy to Abraham, just as Thou didst swear to our fathers in the former days.

units.2 Kings 18:15: Hezekiah gave all the silver found in the Lord’s house and in the treasuries of the king’s house.

units.1 Kings 20:1: Naboth the Jezreelite had a vineyard beside the threshing floor of Ahab king of Samaria.
units.1 Kings 20:2: Ahab said to Naboth, “Give me your vineyard, so it may be a vegetable garden for me, because it is nearer my house. I will give you another vineyard better than it; or, if it pleases you, I will give you silver in exchange for this vineyard of yours, and it will be a vegetable garden for me.”
units.1 Kings 20:3: Naboth said to Ahab, “May my God forbid that I should give you my fathers’ inheritance!”
units.1 Kings 20:4: Ahab’s spirit became troubled. He lay on his bed, covered his face, and ate no bread.
units.1 Kings 20:5: Jezebel his wife came to him and said, “Why is your spirit troubled, and why are you not eating bread?”
units.1 Kings 20:6: He said to her, “I spoke to Naboth the Jezreelite, saying, ‘Give me your vineyard for silver; or, if you wish, I will give you another vineyard in its place.’ But he said, ‘I will not give you my fathers’ inheritance.’”
units.1 Kings 20:7: Jezebel his wife said to him, “Is this how you now act as king over Israel? Rise, eat bread, and be yourself again. I will give you Naboth the Jezreelite’s vineyard.”
units.1 Kings 20:8: She wrote a letter in Ahab’s name, sealed it with his seal, and sent the letter to the elders and free men who lived with Naboth.
units.1 Kings 20:9: It was written in the documents: “Observe a fast and seat Naboth at the head of the people.
units.1 Kings 20:10: Seat two men, sons of lawbreakers, opposite him, and let them testify against him, saying, ‘He has “blessed” God and the king.’ Let them take him out and stone him, and let him die.”
units.1 Kings 20:11: The men of his city—the elders and free men who lived in his city—did as Jezebel had sent to them, as written in the documents she had sent them.
units.1 Kings 20:12: They proclaimed a fast and seated Naboth at the head of the people,
units.1 Kings 20:13: Two men, sons of lawbreakers, came and sat opposite him. They testified against him, saying, “You have ‘blessed’ God and the king.” They took him outside the city and stoned him with stones, and he died.
units.1 Kings 20:14: They sent to Jezebel, saying, “Naboth has been stoned and is dead.”
units.1 Kings 20:15: When Jezebel heard, she said to Ahab, “Rise, take possession of Naboth the Jezreelite’s vineyard, which he did not give you for silver. Naboth is no longer alive; he is dead.”
units.1 Kings 20:16: When Ahab heard that Naboth the Jezreelite was dead, he tore his garments and put on sackcloth. After this, Ahab rose and went down to Naboth the Jezreelite’s vineyard to take possession of it.

full_final_triples.relationship: later identification and citation of the prophet
full_final_triples.rationale: Micah's opening places Michaiah of Morashthi in Hezekiah's reign. Jeremiah identifies Micah the Morathite in that reign and cites the warning found in Micah 3:12. The reign and cited warning support the connection while the supplied name forms remain unchanged.
full_final_triples.source_text: The word of the Lord came to Michaiah of Morashthi in the days of Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, concerning what he saw about Samaria and Jerusalem.

target_units.text: Micah the Morathite lived in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah and said to all Judah’s people: Thus said the Lord: Zion will be plowed as a field, Jerusalem will become an untrodden place, and the house’s mountain a grove of woodland.

Did Hezekiah and all Judah kill him? Was it not that they feared the Lord and entreated the Lord’s face, and the Lord ceased from the evils He spoke against them? And we have done great evils against our own lives!

full_final_triples.relationship: earth summoned before divine testimony and judgment
full_final_triples.rationale: Micah summons the peoples and earth to attend to the Lord's testimony from His holy house. The psalm likewise summons the earth, presents God's manifestation from Zion and calls heaven and earth to His judgment.
full_final_triples.source_text: Hear words, you peoples! Let the earth and everyone in it attend! The Lord will be among you as a testimony, the Lord from His holy house.

From Zion comes the splendor of His beauty; God will come manifestly,
our God, and He will not keep silent; fire will burn before Him, and around Him is a mighty tempest.
He will summon heaven above and the earth, to judge His people.
Gather His holy ones to Him, those who establish His covenant over sacrifices.

full_final_triples.relationship: judgment proceeding from God's dwelling to the earth
full_final_triples.rationale: Micah depicts the Lord coming out of His place and descending upon the earth's heights. Isaiah announces the Lord bringing wrath from the holy place upon earth's inhabitants; both move from God's dwelling to judgment on earth.
full_final_triples.source_text: For look, the Lord is coming out of His place; He will descend and step upon the heights of the earth,

target_units.text: For behold, the Lord brings wrath from the holy place upon those dwelling on the earth. The earth will uncover its blood and will not cover those killed.

full_final_triples.relationship: shaken earth and wax-melting imagery
full_final_triples.rationale: Micah's mountains are shaken and its valleys melt like wax before fire. The psalm likewise describes the shaken earth, with mountains melting like wax before the Lord. The shared shaking and wax imagery preserve the different landscape features named as melting.
full_final_triples.source_text: and the mountains will be shaken beneath Him, and the valleys will melt like wax before fire and like water flowing downhill.

target_units.text: His lightning flashes shone upon the inhabited world; the earth saw and was shaken.
The mountains melted like wax before the Lord, before the Lord of all the earth.

full_final_triples.relationship: Samaria as a focus of Israel's religious offense
full_final_triples.rationale: Micah identifies Samaria with Jacob's impiety. Hosea rebukes Samaria's calf, declares that a craftsman made it and it is no god, and speaks of God's anger. Both locate Israel's offense concretely in Samaria.
full_final_triples.source_text: All this is because of Jacob’s impiety and the sin of Israel’s house. What is Jacob’s impiety? Is it not Samaria? And what is the sin of Judah’s house? Is it not Jerusalem?

target_units.text: Rub away your calf, Samaria! My anger was provoked against them. How long will they be incapable of being cleansed
in Israel? A craftsman made it, and it is no god, because your calf was leading people astray, Samaria.

full_final_triples.relationship: same-book parallel fates of the two capitals
full_final_triples.rationale: Samaria is to become a fruit watcher's hut amid agricultural ground. The later warning similarly makes Jerusalem a fruit watcher's hut and Zion a plowed field, linking the two capitals named in the book's opening through parallel ruin imagery.
full_final_triples.source_text: I will make Samaria a fruit watcher’s hut in a field and a vineyard plantation. I will pull her stones down into a chasm and uncover her foundations.

target_units.text: Therefore, because of you, Zion will be plowed like a field, Jerusalem will be like a fruit watcher’s hut, and the mountain of the house like a forest grove.

full_final_triples.relationship: destruction of idolatrous objects
full_final_triples.rationale: Micah announces the cutting up of Samaria's carved images and obliteration of her idols. Deuteronomy commands the burning of graven images. The shared connection is destruction of the images; Micah specifically assigns the wages to the fire.
full_final_triples.source_text: They will cut up all her carved images and burn all her wages in fire, and I will consign all her idols to obliteration. For she gathered from prostitution wages and amassed from prostitution wages.

full_final_triples.rationale: Micah compares the city's lament with dragons and daughters of sirens. Job calls himself a brother to sirens while describing crying out and song becoming weeping. Both associate lament with sirens, preserving their differing companion animal names.
full_final_triples.source_text: Because of this she will lament and mourn; she will go barefoot and naked. She will make lamentation like dragons and mourning like daughters of sirens.

full_final_triples.rationale: Micah tells those in Gath not to magnify themselves in the midst of the lament. David likewise forbids reporting Israel's defeat in Gath lest foreign daughters rejoice. Both address Gath's possible exultation over Israel's misfortune.
full_final_triples.source_text: You in Gath, do not magnify yourselves! You in Akim, do not rebuild from a house for laughter; sprinkle yourselves with earth in keeping with your laughter.

full_final_triples.rationale: Micah addresses Lachish amid the noise of chariots and horsemen and relates her to Zion's trouble. Kings records an Assyrian force sent from Lachish against Jerusalem. full_final_triples.rationale: Micah commands shaving and shearing in mourning for children taken captive. Amos likewise joins baldness on every head with lamentation and mourning for a beloved one. The shared mourning signs are retained without changing Micah's separate widowhood-and-eagle wording.

full_final_triples.rationale: Micah describes wrongdoers planning evil on their beds before carrying it out. The psalm likewise depicts the lawless person devising lawlessness upon his bed and refusing the good way.
full_final_triples.source_text: They became people planning troubles and working evil on their beds, and at daybreak they carried them out, because they did not raise their hands to God.

full_final_triples.rationale: Micah condemns coveting fields and plundering a person, house and inheritance. Isaiah likewise condemns joining house to house and field to field in order to take from a neighbor.
full_final_triples.source_text: They coveted fields and plundered orphans, oppressed houses and plundered a man and his house, a man and his inheritance.

full_final_triples.relationship: shared pursuit-without-a-pursuer language
full_final_triples.rationale: Micah describes being pursued with no one pursuing. Leviticus' covenant sanctions include fleeing when no one pursues, alongside defeat before enemies. The paradoxical pursuit language is the specific connection.

full_final_triples.rationale: Micah promises to gather Israel's remaining ones, compares them with sheep in affliction and a flock within its resting place, and says they will leap out from among people. full_final_triples.relationship: leaders' responsibility for justice
full_final_triples.rationale: Micah asks Israel's authorities whether they ought to know justice. Deuteronomy directs appointed judges and officers to judge the people with righteous judgment, supplying the explicit responsibility challenged by the question.

full_final_triples.relationship: opposition between corrupt preferences and the call to good
full_final_triples.rationale: Micah accuses leaders of hating good and seeking evil. Amos calls for seeking good rather than evil and restoring judgment, directly opposing the preferences Micah condemns.

full_final_triples.relationship: shared imagery of devouring the people
full_final_triples.rationale: Micah describes the people's flesh treated as meat for a cooking pot. The psalm similarly accuses lawless people of devouring the people like a meal of bread. Both use eating imagery to portray abuse of the people.
full_final_triples.source_text: Just as they ate the flesh of My people, flayed their skins from their bones, crushed their bones and divided them into pieces like flesh for a cauldron and meat for a cooking pot,

target_units.text: Will all those who practice lawlessness not know? Those who devour my people as a meal of bread did not call upon the Lord.

full_final_triples.relationship: violence followed by rejected prayer
full_final_triples.rationale: Micah says the Lord will not hear the cry of those who acted wickedly against the people and will turn His face away. Isaiah likewise says He will turn His eyes away and refuse multiplied supplications because their hands are full of blood.

full_final_triples.relationship: corrupt prophetic pronouncements tied to food
full_final_triples.rationale: Micah's misleading prophets proclaim peace when their mouths are supplied and raise war when they are not. Ezekiel condemns profaning God through vain pronouncements for barley and scraps of bread; both connect deceptive prophetic activity with food received.

full_final_triples.relationship: shared judgment imagery of lost daylight
full_final_triples.rationale: Micah announces night in place of vision and sunset over the prophets. Amos similarly announces the sun setting at midday and light becoming dark during daytime. Micah applies the darkness specifically to the prophets' loss of vision.

full_final_triples.rationale: Micah announces shame for dream-seers and mockery for diviners. Zechariah likewise says prophets will be ashamed because of their visions when they prophesy.

target_units.text: to destroy the Assyrians from My land and from My mountains. They will become a trampling place; their yoke will be removed from them, and their glory removed from the shoulders.”

full_final_triples.relationship: dew imagery connected with Israel and the Lord
full_final_triples.rationale: Micah compares Jacob's remnant among the peoples with dew falling from the Lord. Hosea promises that the Lord will be like dew to Israel. Both connect Israel and dew with the Lord, while assigning the image differently.
full_final_triples.source_text: Jacob’s remnant will be among the nations, amid many peoples, like dew falling from the Lord and like lambs upon couch grass, so that no one may be gathered or stand among the sons of humankind.

target_units.text: I will be like dew to Israel; he will blossom like a lily and put down his roots like Lebanon.

full_final_triples.relationship: shared lion imagery with no rescuer
full_final_triples.rationale: Micah depicts the remnant as a lion seizing among flocks with no one to deliver. Hosea likewise uses a lion comparison and seizure with no one to rescue. Micah applies the image to the remnant; Hosea applies it to the Lord's judgment against Judah.
full_final_triples.source_text: Jacob’s remnant will be among the nations, amid many peoples, like a lion among beasts in the forest and like a young lion among flocks of sheep, which passes through, separates and seizes, with no one to deliver.

target_units.text: For I am like a panther to Ephraim and like a lion to Judah’s house. I seize and will go away and take, and there will be no one to rescue.

full_final_triples.relationship: hands over enemies as victory imagery
full_final_triples.rationale: Micah promises the hand raised over afflicting enemies. Jacob's blessing of Judah likewise places his hands upon his enemies' backs, using the position of the hand to express victory over opponents.
full_final_triples.source_text: Your hand will be raised above those afflicting you, and all your enemies will be destroyed.

target_units.text: “Judah, may your brothers praise you; your hands shall be upon the backs of your enemies, and your father’s sons shall bow down to you.

full_final_triples.relationship: parallel removal of horses and chariots
full_final_triples.rationale: Micah announces destruction of the people's horses and chariots. Zechariah likewise announces the destruction of chariots from Ephraim and the horse from Jerusalem, placing that removal beside peace and the coming king's rule.
full_final_triples.source_text: “On that day,” says the Lord, “I will destroy your horses from your midst and destroy your chariots,

target_units.text: He will destroy chariots from Ephraim and the horse from Jerusalem; the battle bow will be destroyed, and abundance and peace from the nations. He will rule waters as far as the sea and the earth’s river outlets.

full_final_triples.relationship: judgment on fortified cities
full_final_triples.rationale: Micah promises to destroy cities and remove strongholds. Hosea specifically condemns Judah's multiplication of walled cities and announces fire that will devour their foundations.
full_final_triples.source_text: and I will destroy the cities of your land and remove all your strongholds.

target_units.text: Israel forgot his Maker, and they built sacred precincts; Judah multiplied walled cities. I will send fire into his cities, and it will devour their foundations.

full_final_triples.relationship: removal of forbidden sorcery and divination
full_final_triples.rationale: Micah announces removal of sorceries and utterers of oracles. Deuteronomy forbids sorcery, divination and related practices among Israel and contrasts the nations' reliance on them with the Lord's instruction.
full_final_triples.source_text: I will remove your sorceries from your hands, and there will be no utterers of oracles among you.

target_units.text: There shall not be found among you one who purifies his son or his daughter by fire, or practises divination, or interprets spoken omens, or observes auguries, or works sorcery,
or chants spells, or is a medium, or observes portents, or inquires of the dead.
For everyone who does these things is an abomination unto the Lord your God; for because of these abominations the Lord shall destroy them from before you.
You shall be perfect before the Lord your God.
For these nations whose possession you inherit hearken unto omens and divinations; but the Lord your God has not granted you so to do.

full_final_triples.relationship: parallel destruction of images and pillars
full_final_triples.rationale: Micah promises destruction of carved images and pillars and an end to bowing to handmade works. Deuteronomy commands the breaking of pillars and burning of graven images, sharing the elimination of these objects of worship.
full_final_triples.source_text: I will destroy your carved images and pillars from your midst, and you will certainly no longer bow down to the works of your hands.

target_units.text: And you shall pull down their altars, and break their pillars, and cut down their sacred groves, and burn the graven images of their gods with fire; and their name shall perish from that place.

full_final_triples.relationship: parallel cutting down of sacred groves
full_final_triples.rationale: Micah promises to cut down the groves from the people's midst. Deuteronomy specifically commands cutting down sacred groves along with destroying other objects of foreign worship.
full_final_triples.source_text: I will cut down your groves from your midst and obliterate your cities.

target_units.text: And you shall pull down their altars, and break their pillars, and cut down their sacred groves, and burn the graven images of their gods with fire; and their name shall perish from that place.

full_final_triples.relationship: parallel wrath against nations
full_final_triples.rationale: Micah announces vengeance in anger and wrath among disobedient nations. Isaiah summons nations to hear that the Lord's wrath and anger are against them for destruction, matching the announced agent, recipients and punitive anger.
full_final_triples.source_text: I will execute vengeance in anger and wrath among the nations because they did not obey.”

target_units.text: Draw near, nations, and hear, rulers! Let the earth and those in it hear, the inhabited world and the people in it!
For the Lord’s wrath is against all nations, and anger against their number, to destroy them and hand them over to slaughter.

full_final_triples.relationship: creation summoned to hear the divine case
full_final_triples.rationale: Micah calls for the mountains and hills to hear the word in the setting of judgment. Moses likewise calls heaven and earth to hear his words, using creation as the audience to a declaration concerning God and His people.
full_final_triples.source_text: Hear now the word of the Lord. The Lord said: “Rise, enter into judgment before the mountains, and let the hills hear your voice.”

target_units.text: Give ear, O heaven, and I will speak; and let the earth hear the words of my mouth.

full_final_triples.relationship: creation as witness to God's judgment of His people
full_final_triples.rationale: Micah calls the hills, ravines and earth's foundations to hear the Lord's case with Israel. The psalm likewise summons heaven and earth to God's judgment of His covenant people and declares God the judge.
full_final_triples.source_text: Hear, hills, the Lord’s judgment, and you ravines, foundations of the earth! For the Lord has a case against His people, and He will argue it with Israel.

target_units.text: He will summon heaven above and the earth, to judge His people.
Gather His holy ones to Him, those who establish His covenant over sacrifices.
The heavens will announce His righteousness, for God is judge. Diapsalma.

full_final_triples.relationship: parallel divine question about an alleged offense
full_final_triples.rationale: The Lord asks His people what He has done to grieve or trouble them. Jeremiah similarly asks what offense their fathers found in Him that led them away, framing the people's departure against God's challenge to name His wrongdoing.
full_final_triples.source_text: “My people, what have I done to you? How have I grieved you, or how have I troubled you? Answer Me!

target_units.text: Thus says the Lord: What offense did your fathers find in Me, that they withdrew far from Me, followed futile things and became futile?

full_final_triples.relationship: explicit recollection of deliverance from slavery
full_final_triples.rationale: Micah recalls the Lord bringing Israel from Egypt and redeeming them from the house of slavery. Exodus uses that same Egypt-and-house-of-bondage description in the Lord's declaration introducing the commandments.
full_final_triples.source_text: For I brought you up from Egypt’s land and redeemed you from the house of slavery. I sent Moses, Aaron and Miriam before you.

target_units.text: “I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.

full_final_triples.relationship: explicit recollection of Balak and Balaam
full_final_triples.rationale: Micah commands remembrance of Balak's plan and Balaam's answer. Numbers records Balak summoning Balaam to curse Jacob, Balaam's refusal to curse those God does not curse, and Balak's complaint that a blessing was given instead.
full_final_triples.source_text: My people, remember what Balak king of Moab planned against you and what Balaam son of Beor answered him, from the rushes to Galgal, so that the Lord’s righteousness may be known.”

target_units.text: And God's Spirit came upon him, and he took up his parable and said: Balak summoned me from Mesopotamia, the king of Moab from the eastern mountains: Come, curse Jacob for me; come, call down a curse on Israel for me.
Why should I curse whom the Lord does not curse? Why should I call down a curse on whom God does not curse?
From the tops of mountains I shall see them, and from the hills I shall observe them. Behold, a people who will dwell alone, not counted among the nations.
Who has measured Jacob’s seed exactly, and who will count Israel's clans? May my soul die among righteous souls, and may my seed be like their seed!
And Balak said to Balaam: What have you done to me? I summoned you to curse my enemies, and look, you have pronounced a blessing!
And Balaam said to Balak: Must I not take care to speak what God puts in my mouth?

full_final_triples.relationship: questioning the sufficiency of animal offerings
full_final_triples.rationale: Micah asks whether burnt offerings and calves can be the means of taking hold of the Lord. The psalm likewise discusses continual burnt offerings, refuses calves and questions whether God eats bulls' flesh, directing attention beyond merely supplying sacrificial animals.
full_final_triples.source_text: With what shall I take hold of the Lord and grasp my God Most High? Shall I take hold of Him with whole burnt offerings, with year-old calves?

target_units.text: I will not rebuke you concerning your sacrifices; your burnt offerings are continually before Me.
I will not receive calves from your house or young goats from your flocks.
For all the forest’s wild animals are Mine, beasts on the mountains and cattle.
I know all the birds of heaven, and the field’s beauty is with Me.
If I become hungry, I will certainly not tell you, for the inhabited world and its fullness are Mine.
Will I eat bulls’ flesh or drink goats’ blood?

full_final_triples.relationship: sacrificial abundance contrasted with obedience
full_final_triples.rationale: Micah asks whether thousands of rams can satisfy the Lord before stating what He seeks in the next verse. Samuel explicitly places listening and obedience above sacrifice and the fat of rams.
full_final_triples.source_text: Will the Lord receive with thousands of rams or with ten thousands of fat-rich torrents? Shall I give my firstborn offspring for impieties, the fruit of my body for the sin of my life?

target_units.text: Samuel said, “Are whole burnt offerings and sacrifices as desirable to the Lord as listening to the Lord’s voice? Behold, obedience is better than sacrifice, and attentiveness than the fat of rams.

full_final_triples.relationship: firstborn sacrifice considered against the rejection of child offerings
full_final_triples.rationale: Micah asks whether a firstborn child could be given for sin, followed by the Lord's ethical requirements. Deuteronomy explicitly rejects the nations' burning of sons and daughters as practices the Lord hates, bearing on the proposed child offering.
full_final_triples.source_text: Will the Lord receive with thousands of rams or with ten thousands of fat-rich torrents? Shall I give my firstborn offspring for impieties, the fruit of my body for the sin of my life?

target_units.text: You shall not do so unto the Lord your God; for the abominations which the Lord hated they did unto their gods, for they burn their sons and their daughters with fire unto their gods.

full_final_triples.relationship: parallel statement of what the Lord requires
full_final_triples.rationale: Micah asks what the Lord seeks and names justice, mercy and readiness to walk with Him. Deuteronomy likewise asks what He requires and names fear, walking in His ways, love, service and keeping His commands.
full_final_triples.source_text: Has it been declared to you, O man, what is good? Or what does the Lord seek from you, except to do justice, and to love mercy, and to be ready to walk with the Lord your God?

target_units.text: And now, O Israel, what does the Lord your God require of you, but to fear the Lord your God, to walk in all His ways, and to love Him, and to serve the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul,
to keep the commandments of the Lord your God, and His ordinances which I command you this day, that it may be well with you?

full_final_triples.relationship: justice and mercy as weighty requirements
full_final_triples.rationale: Micah identifies doing justice and loving mercy among what God seeks. Jesus likewise names justice and mercy among the Law's weightier matters, contrasting their neglect with meticulous tithing.
full_final_triples.source_text: Has it been declared to you, O man, what is good? Or what does the Lord seek from you, except to do justice, and to love mercy, and to be ready to walk with the Lord your God?

target_units.text: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you tithe mint, dill, and cumin, but have left aside the weightier matters of the Law: justice, mercy, and faithfulness! These you ought to have done without leaving those aside.

full_final_triples.relationship: salvation promised to those who fear the Lord
full_final_triples.rationale: Micah says the Lord will save those who fear His name. The psalm likewise says He hears and saves those who fear Him, directly joining reverence and rescue.
full_final_triples.source_text: The Lord’s voice will be called to the city, and He will save those who fear His name. “Hear, tribe! And who will adorn a city?

target_units.text: He will fulfill the will of those who fear Him; He will hear their plea and save them.

full_final_triples.relationship: treasure and the lawless person
full_final_triples.rationale: Micah exposes a lawless person's house storing lawless treasures. Proverbs warns that treasures do not profit lawless people and contrasts them with righteousness that rescues from death.
full_final_triples.source_text: Is there not fire, and a lawless person’s house storing lawless treasures, and injustice with insolence?

target_units.text: Treasures will not profit lawless people, but righteousness will rescue from death.

full_final_triples.relationship: deceptive weights opposed to the legal standard
full_final_triples.rationale: Micah questions whether a lawless person can be justified with deceptive weights in a pouch. Deuteronomy expressly forbids differing weights in the pouch, requires just weights and condemns the injustice.
full_final_triples.source_text: Will a lawless person be justified with a balance and deceptive weights in a pouch?

target_units.text: You shall not have in your pouch differing weights, a great and a small.
You shall not have in your house differing measures, a great and a small.
You shall have a true and just weight, and you shall have a true and just measure, that your days may be long upon the land which the Lord your God gives you for a possession.
For everyone who does these things, everyone who does injustice, is an abomination unto the Lord your God.

full_final_triples.relationship: wealth associated with deceit and impiety
full_final_triples.rationale: Micah links accumulated wealth with impiety and the inhabitants' false speech. Jeremiah likewise describes houses filled with deceit whose owners became great and rich, followed by their failure to judge rightly and the promise of visitation.
full_final_triples.source_text: From these they filled their wealth with impiety; those inhabiting her spoke falsehoods, and their tongue was exalted in their mouth.

target_units.text: For impious people were found among My people, and they set traps to destroy men and were catching them.
Like a set trap full of birds, so their houses are full of deceit; therefore they became great and rich.
And they transgressed judgment; they did not judge an orphan’s case, and they were not judging a widow’s case.
Shall I not visit for these things? says the Lord. Or will not My soul take vengeance on such a nation?

full_final_triples.relationship: punishment for sins preceding agricultural deprivation
full_final_triples.rationale: Micah announces striking and obliteration because of sins, followed by hunger and crop losses. Leviticus similarly announces discipline for sins followed by ineffective labor and land and trees failing to yield.
full_final_triples.source_text: And I will begin to strike you; I will obliterate you because of your sins.

target_units.text: And if up to this point you do not obey Me, I will discipline you seven times more for your sins.
And I will shatter the arrogance of your pride, and make your heaven iron, and your land as bronze;
and your strength shall be in vain. Your land shall not yield its seed, and the tree of your field shall not yield its fruit.

full_final_triples.relationship: shared curse of eating without satisfaction
full_final_triples.rationale: Micah says the people will eat but not be filled. Leviticus uses the same eating-without-being-filled warning within the covenant's scarcity-of-bread sanctions.
full_final_triples.source_text: You will eat but certainly not be filled. It will grow dark within you and turn aside, and you will certainly not be saved; whoever is saved will be handed over to the sword.

target_units.text: When I afflict you with a scarcity of bread, ten women shall bake your bread in one oven and give back your bread by weight. You shall eat and in no wise be filled.

full_final_triples.relationship: parallel loss of grain, wine and olive yield
full_final_triples.rationale: Micah announces sowing without reaping, pressing olives without anointing and pressing wine without drinking. Deuteronomy likewise warns of failed grain yield, vineyards whose wine is not drunk and olives that give no oil for anointing.
full_final_triples.source_text: You will sow but certainly not reap; you will press olives but certainly not anoint yourself with oil, and you will press wine, but you shall certainly not drink it. The ordinances of My people will be obliterated.

target_units.text: You shall carry much seed into the field, and gather little; for the locust shall devour it.
You shall plant a vineyard and dress it, but shall neither drink wine nor rejoice in it; for the worm shall devour it.
You shall have olive trees throughout all your borders, but shall not anoint yourself with oil; for your olives shall fall away.

full_final_triples.relationship: shared imagery of an absent fruit crop
full_final_triples.rationale: Micah laments the lack of an available cluster at the vintage. Jeremiah likewise describes vines without grapes and fig trees without figs. Both portray fruitlessness in passages that also address the people's wrongdoing.
full_final_triples.source_text: Alas! I have become like someone gathering stubble at harvest and a gleaning at vintage, with no cluster available to eat the first fruits. Alas, my soul,

target_units.text: and they will gather their produce, says the Lord. There is no grape on the vines and no figs on the fig trees, and the leaves have fallen.

full_final_triples.relationship: shared lament for vanished faithfulness
full_final_triples.rationale: Micah laments that the devout person has perished and no one acts rightly among people. The psalm similarly cries that the holy one is gone and truths have diminished, followed by deceit toward neighbors.
full_final_triples.source_text: for the devout person has perished from the earth, and no one acts rightly among people. They all litigate for bloodshed; each crushes his neighbor with crushing.

target_units.text: Save me, Lord, for the holy one is gone; for truths have become few among the sons of men.
Each spoke empty things to his neighbor; deceitful lips spoke with a heart and a heart.

full_final_triples.relationship: shared moth-consumption imagery of loss
full_final_triples.rationale: Micah pictures removal of the people's good things with a moth eating away. Isaiah likewise speaks of wool eaten by a moth, in contrast to God's lasting righteousness and salvation. The connection is the consuming-moth image; Micah's other wording remains unchanged.
full_final_triples.source_text: their good things like a moth eating away and walking upon a measuring rod on the day of watching. Woe, woe! Your punishments have arrived; now they will weep.

target_units.text: Listen to Me, you who know judgment, My people with My law in your heart. Do not fear people’s reproach or be overcome by their contempt.
For a garment will be consumed by time, and wool eaten by a moth. But My righteousness will last for ever, and My salvation through generations of generations.”

full_final_triples.relationship: parallel warning against trust in familiar companions
full_final_triples.rationale: Micah warns against confidence in friends and even disclosure to a bed companion. Jeremiah likewise warns people to guard against neighbors and not trust brothers because friends act deceitfully.
full_final_triples.source_text: Do not put confidence in friends or hope in leaders. With your bed companion, beware of entrusting anything to her.

target_units.text: Each of you, guard against his neighbor, and do not put trust in their brothers, because every brother will trip with the heel, and every friend will walk deceitfully.
Each will mock his friend; they certainly will not speak truth. Their tongue has learned to speak false things; they did wrong and did not cease turning back.

full_final_triples.relationship: explicitly corresponding household-division language
full_final_triples.rationale: Micah lists son against father, daughter against mother, daughter-in-law against mother-in-law, and enemies within the household. Matthew reproduces the same family divisions and household-enemy statement in Jesus' description of division associated with His coming.
full_final_triples.source_text: For a son dishonors his father, a daughter will rise against her mother, a daughter-in-law will rise against her mother-in-law; a man’s enemies are all the men in his house.

target_units.text: For I came to divide a man against his father, a daughter against her mother, and a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law,
and a person’s enemies will be the members of his own household.

full_final_triples.relationship: waiting for the Lord and being heard
full_final_triples.rationale: The speaker in Micah resolves to wait upon God the Savior and expects Him to listen. The psalm recalls waiting patiently for the Lord and being heard, giving an answered-prayer counterpart to that expectation.
full_final_triples.source_text: But I will look toward the Lord; I will wait upon God my Savior. My God will listen to me.

target_units.text: I waited patiently for the Lord; He attended to me and heard my supplication.

full_final_triples.relationship: falling, rising and forbidden enemy rejoicing
full_final_triples.rationale: The speaker in Micah tells the enemy not to rejoice at the speaker's fall because rising will follow. Proverbs likewise says the righteous fall and rise and then forbids rejoicing over an enemy's fall.
full_final_triples.source_text: Do not rejoice over me, my enemy, because I have fallen! I will rise, for if I sit in darkness, the Lord will shine for me.

target_units.text: for the righteous will fall seven times and rise, but the impious will grow weak amid evils.
If your enemy falls, do not rejoice over him, and at his tripping do not lift yourself up,
for the Lord will see, and it will not please Him, and He will turn His wrath away from him.

full_final_triples.relationship: acknowledgment of sin amid divine displeasure
full_final_triples.rationale: The speaker in Micah bears the Lord's anger because of acknowledged sin, while awaiting vindication. Lamentations similarly questions grumbling over one's sin, calls for return to the Lord and acknowledges godlessness and unappeased divine displeasure.
full_final_triples.source_text: I will bear the Lord’s anger, for I sinned against Him, until He vindicates my case. He will execute my judgment and bring me out into the light; I will see His righteousness.

target_units.text: Why should a living person grumble, a man concerning his sin?
Our way was searched and examined; let us return to the Lord.
Let us lift our hearts upon our hands to the Exalted One in heaven.
We have sinned and acted godlessly, and Thou wast not propitiated.

full_final_triples.relationship: shared taunt about God's whereabouts
full_final_triples.rationale: Micah records an enemy asking where the speaker's God is. The psalmist likewise hears the repeated taunt, Where is your God, while suffering in tears. Both place that question in the mouth of those aggravating the afflicted person's distress.
full_final_triples.source_text: My enemy will see and clothe herself in shame, she who says to me, “Where is the Lord your God?” My eyes will look upon her; now she will become a trampling place like mud in the streets

target_units.text: My tears became my bread day and night, while it is said to me every day, “Where is your God?”

full_final_triples.relationship: judgment according to the fruits of conduct
full_final_triples.rationale: Micah attributes the land's obliteration to the fruits of its inhabitants' practices. Jeremiah states that the Lord gives to each according to their ways and the fruits of their practices, articulating the principle behind such recompense.
full_final_triples.source_text: The land will become an obliteration together with those inhabiting it, from the fruits of their practices.

target_units.text: I, the Lord, examine hearts and test kidneys, to give each according to his ways and the fruits of his practices.

full_final_triples.relationship: prayer to Israel's divine shepherd
full_final_triples.rationale: Micah asks God to shepherd the people, described as the sheep of His inheritance. The psalm likewise addresses the One shepherding Israel and guiding Joseph like sheep, then asks Him to come and save.
full_final_triples.source_text: Shepherd Thy people with Thy rod, the sheep of Thine inheritance, camping by themselves in a forest amid Carmel. They will graze in Bashan and Gilead as in the days of old.

target_units.text: Thou who shepherdest Israel, pay attention, Thou who guidest Joseph like sheep; Thou who sittest upon the cherubim, appear.
Before Ephraim and Benjamin and Manasseh, rouse Thy dominion, and come to save us.
God, turn us back; make Thy face shine, and we shall be saved.

full_final_triples.relationship: explicit recollection of the exodus as a pattern of wonders
full_final_triples.rationale: Micah promises wonders like those seen at the departure from Egypt. Exodus narrates the Lord rescuing Israel from the Egyptians and Israel seeing His great hand, providing the recalled deliverance pattern.
full_final_triples.source_text: And as in the days of your departure from Egypt, you will see wonderful things.

target_units.text: The Lord rescued Israel that day from the Egyptians’ hand, and Israel saw the Egyptians dead on the seashore.
Israel saw the great hand in what the Lord had done to the Egyptians. The people feared the Lord and trusted God and His attendant Moses.

full_final_triples.relationship: nations seeing and mouths falling silent
full_final_triples.rationale: Micah depicts nations seeing God's work and putting hands over their mouths. Isaiah likewise depicts nations marveling and kings closing their mouths as they see what had not been proclaimed to them. Both portray a silenced response to what they witness, in differing prophetic settings.
full_final_triples.source_text: Nations will see and be ashamed of all their strength. They will place hands over their mouth; their ears will be deafened.

target_units.text: so many nations will marvel at him, and kings will close their mouths. For those to whom he was not proclaimed will see, and those who have not heard will understand.

full_final_triples.relationship: shared serpent-and-earth humiliation imagery
full_final_triples.rationale: Micah compares the nations licking dust with snakes moving along the ground. Genesis condemns the serpent to go on breast and belly and eat earth. The connection is the degrading serpent-and-earth image, not an identification of the nations with that individual serpent.
full_final_triples.source_text: They will lick dust like snakes dragging along the earth; they will be thrown into turmoil in their confinement. They will be astonished at the Lord our God and fear Thee.

target_units.text: And the Lord God said to the serpent: Because you have done this, cursed are you above all cattle and all the wild beasts of the earth. Upon your breast and belly you shall go, and earth you shall eat all the days of your life.

full_final_triples.relationship: shared dust-licking image of humbled opponents
full_final_triples.rationale: Micah depicts the nations licking dust and fearing God. The royal psalm likewise describes enemies licking dust, with kings bowing and nations serving, using the same action to express humbled opposition.
full_final_triples.source_text: They will lick dust like snakes dragging along the earth; they will be thrown into turmoil in their confinement. They will be astonished at the Lord our God and fear Thee.

target_units.text: Ethiopians will fall before him, and his enemies will lick dust.
kings of Tarshish and the islands will offer gifts; kings of the Arabians and Saba will bring gifts.
And all kings will bow before him; all nations will serve him.

full_final_triples.relationship: shared question of God's incomparability
full_final_triples.rationale: Micah asks who is a God like the Lord in the context of mercy and forgiveness. The exodus song similarly asks who is like the Lord among the gods, praising His wondrous works. The shared rhetorical question introduces praise with different immediate emphases.
full_final_triples.source_text: Who is a God like Thee, removing injustices and passing over impieties for the remaining ones of His inheritance? He did not retain His anger as a testimony, because He desires mercy.

target_units.text: Who is like Thee among the gods, O Lord? Who is like Thee, glorified among the holy ones, marvellous in glories, working wonders?

full_final_triples.relationship: shared mercy and removal of wrongdoing
full_final_triples.rationale: Micah praises God for removing injustices, passing over impieties and desiring mercy. Exodus's proclamation of His name likewise emphasizes mercy and the taking away of lawlessness, injustice and sins.
full_final_triples.source_text: Who is a God like Thee, removing injustices and passing over impieties for the remaining ones of His inheritance? He did not retain His anger as a testimony, because He desires mercy.

target_units.text: The Lord passed before him and proclaimed, “The Lord God, compassionate and merciful, slow to anger, abundant in mercy and true,

preserving righteousness and showing mercy to thousands, taking away lawlessness, injustice, and sins, yet not cleansing the guilty, bringing the fathers’ lawlessness upon children and children’s children to the third and fourth generation.”

full_final_triples.relationship: spatial imagery of sins removed from the people
full_final_triples.rationale: Micah pictures injustices sunk and sins thrown into the sea's depths. The psalm describes lawless deeds removed as far as east from west. Both use distance or depth to portray God's removal of the people's wrongdoing.
